item.title: REVIEW: Talk Is Free’s Company is valiant but imperfect
item.description: Playing at The Theatre Centre, it’s an entertaining staging that, like its central character, is still waiting to completely connect.

item.title: REVIEW: In Tarragon and Native Earth’s Mischief, the jokes aren’t the point
item.description: Mischief may not fully cohere into a singular statement, but it leaves behind something quieter and more human: the feeling of having spent time inside a community, listening to its jokes, its arguments, and its silences. It is a play full of questions — some answered, many not — and it trusts the audience enough to live with that uncertainty.

item.title: REVIEW: Canadian Stage’s A Doll’s House weighs the burden of our inherited roles
item.description: Hailey Gillis' Nora is not so much a doll as she is a gifted actor, reeling through daffy comedy, seductive calculation, and suicidal ideation with ease.

item.title: REVIEW: Primary Trust harnesses anxiety for good at London’s Grand Theatre
item.description: Eboni Booth's Pulitzer Prize-winning Primary Trust invites its audience to visualize hopeful futures rather than disasters. This tender production, directed by Cherissa Richards, proposes that imagining such a future is the first step to achieving it.

item.title: REVIEW: Two critics compare reactions to TIFT’s new musical All the Cows Are Dead
item.description: Liam wrote about observing the production's rehearsal process. Shivani viewed the musical without any insider knowledge. On the way home from seeing the show in Barrie, they discuss.

item.title: Lester Trips wants Toronto theatre creators to ‘make it nasty’
item.description: "It doesn’t matter how many reels of a hamster falling out of its cage set to the Requiem I see: The music still hits," says Lauren Gillis. "We joke that the logline for Honey I’m Home is 'normie drone has menty-b from VR Zoom with her own living room.'"

item.title: REVIEW: COC’s elegantly bleak Rigoletto is no laughing matter
item.description: As Rigoletto wept, I became distracted by a lone petal belatedly descending from above. An accident, certainly, but one that offered a reminder of opera’s unpredictable magic: that, even among the grandest of designs, a performance’s final form depends upon these ephemeral moments one calls fate.

item.title: REVIEW: Shakespeare BASH’d brings focus to the mystifying Troilus and Cressida
item.description: This spare, thoughtful staging prioritizes a clarity of text that comes through even when the script’s overall trajectory is less than clear.

item.title: A look inside the flourishing creative life of playwright-actor Pamela Mala Sinha (part one)
item.description: When I learned that the acclaimed artist would be having an action-packed start to 2026, I decided to document this busy period in a trilogy of articles.

item.title: TO Live to present Recirquel’s Paradisum in Toronto
item.description: Next week, a circus-dance hybrid will swing into the Bluma Appel Theatre as part of TO Live’s 2025-26 season.
